name: The Tholos
summary: The beehive tomb's chamber: four rings of corbelled ashlar stepping inward overhead, a king on his bier under a gold mask, gold cups set out for him.
description: The tholos is the last room of the tomb and the reason for all the others. Its ashlar courses were laid in rings, each ring a hand's breadth further in than the one below, so the walls lean over you as they rise toward a dome that closes somewhere out of sight; behind them the earth of the mound is packed solid to the old walls. The rings break at the four doorways where the diggers came through. In the north-east corner the king lies on a painted bier with a beaten gold mask over his face, a tripod brazier still standing at his feet. Across from him an offering table holds his cups, and a bronze-bound chest in the south-west keeps what his heirs did not dare to take back. Everything in here was meant to be left alone, which is why it is still here.
build: Shell: the kit's Crypt shell, 12.0 × 12.0 × 0.30 m slab, 0.50 m limestone walls 3.00 m clear, 0.45 m ashlar capstone band, an archway 2.60 × 2.16 m centred on every wall.

Corbelled courses: four rings of ashlar, each 0.65 m high, inner radius 4.90 / 4.55 / 4.20 / 3.85 m from the cell centre, bottoms at 0.00 / 0.65 / 1.30 / 1.95 m above the floor; the top course ends at 2.60 m.
Arcs: each ring built as four arcs, one per quadrant, from 28° to 62° off the nearer axis in six facets (45° is a facet corner); the gaps at the axes leave the archways and the clear cross open.

Fill: behind each arc the course runs solid out to 0.02 m short of the walls, into the corner, so from above the stepped treads read as the mound's packing; one stepped mesh per quadrant, courses sharing their edges.

Bier (NE): ashlar block 1.80 × 0.70 × 0.50 m at (2.70, 2.35), long axis east–west, a haematite band 1.82 × 0.72 × 0.06 m round it at 0.38 m, a linen shroud 1.70 × 0.60 × 0.06 m on top and a gold death-mask 0.22 × 0.18 × 0.05 m at the head (east) end; it sits under the upper courses' overhang with 0.74 m to spare.
Tripod brazier (NE): the Age's bronze tripod, legs 0.90 m, bowl r 0.30 m, at (2.00, 3.35), at the bier's foot.
Offering table (NW): ashlar, 0.90 × 0.60 m, top at 0.70 m, at (−2.60, 2.60), three gold cups on it.
Chest (SW): timber, 1.00 × 0.60 × 0.55 m with a 0.05 m bronze lid band, at (−2.80, −2.30); two amphorae 0.62 m beside it at (−2.00, −3.20) and (−2.60, −3.40).
Standing brazier (SE): the kit brazier in bronze with a haematite fire bed, at (2.70, −2.70).
Paint: alternate courses a shade apart so the rings read from above (albedo only).
sockets: Archway ×4, centred on each wall: 2.60 × 2.16 m (Crypt), all open
Bier top: loot anchor at 0.86 m
Tripod bowl, offering table and chest lid: loot anchors

materials.name: Dressed ashlar
materials.notes: Courses, bier, offering table, capstone band.

materials.name: Bronze
materials.notes: Braziers and the chest's lid band.

gameplay: The final chamber: the death-mask on the bier is the Bronze crypt's headline loot.
The overhanging rings make the corners dark nooks under a low stone ceiling; the cross stays open end to end.
Four loot anchors across three quadrants, so a thief crosses the room's centre to clear it; the tripod is bronze worth carrying.
